provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Singing simple songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing simple songs.
The pupils should be able to perform action songs in groups.
Introduction:
Today we will learn new songs. We know many songs already.
Content:
We will sing songs with actions. Songs help us learn and have fun.
We will sing in groups. Each group will take turns to sing.
Example: Clap your hands stomp your feet.
Class activity:
The class will form groups and sing action songs together.
Evaluation questions:
What songs do you know?
Can you show me how to clap?
How does singing make you feel?
Summary:
Singing songs is fun and helps us learn together.

topics.title: Drawing simple objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw a ball and cup.
The pupils should be able to colour their drawings neatly.
Introduction:
We have learned about colours. Today we will draw objects.
Content:
We will draw a ball and a cup. A ball is round. A cup has a handle.
We will use pencils to draw first. Then we will use crayons to colour.
Example: Draw a circle for the ball. Draw a shape with a handle for the cup.
Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a ball and cup on paper. Then colour them neatly.
Evaluation questions:
What shape is a ball?
What part does a cup have?
How do you hold a crayon?
Summary:
Drawing objects helps us learn about shapes and colours.

topics.title: Colouring pictures
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to colour inside the lines.
The pupils should be able to enjoy using different colours.
Introduction:
We know how to draw. Today we will learn to colour pictures.
Content:
Colouring means adding colour to drawings. We must stay inside the lines.
We have many colours like red blue green yellow and brown.
Example: Colour the grass green and the sky blue.
Class activity:
Pupils will colour a picture of a house with a garden.
Evaluation questions:
What colours do you like?
Where should we colour?
Why do we stay inside the lines?
Summary:
Colouring pictures is fun when we stay inside the lines.

topics.title: Clapping rhythms
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to clap simple beats.
The pupils should be able to follow the teacher's rhythm.
Introduction:
We use music in our culture. Today we will learn clapping rhythms.
Content:
Rhythm is the beat in music. We can make rhythm by clapping our hands.
We will clap slowly and then fast. We will clap together.
Example: Clap-clap-pause. Clap-clap-pause.
Class activity:
The teacher will show a rhythm. Pupils will copy the rhythm.
Evaluation questions:
What is rhythm?
Can you clap fast?
Can you clap slow?
Summary:
Clapping rhythms helps us feel the beat in music.

topics.title: Traditional dances
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to watch simple dance steps.
The pupils should be able to try the dance steps.
Introduction:
Nigeria has many beautiful dances. Today we will learn simple steps.
Content:
Traditional dances show our culture. We will learn steps from dances like Ekombi or Agba.
First we watch the teacher. Then we try the steps together.
Example: Step left step right clap hands.
Class activity:
The class will follow the teacher to do simple dance steps.
Evaluation questions:
What dances do you know?
Can you show me a step?
Why do people dance?
Summary:
Traditional dances help us learn about our culture.

topics.title: Moulding with clay
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mould balls and snakes from clay.
The pupils should be able to mould simple shapes.
Introduction:\ Today we will use clay to make things. Clay is soft and can be shaped.
Content:
We will make balls and snakes from clay. We will roll the clay in our hands.
We can also make shapes like circles and squares.
Example: Roll clay between palms to make a ball. Roll clay to make a long snake.
Class activity:
Pupils will make balls snakes and simple shapes from clay.
Evaluation questions:
What can we make with clay?
How do we make a ball?
What shape is a snake?
Summary:
Moulding clay helps us make many different things.

topics.title: Craft: paper tearing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tear paper into small pieces.
The pupils should be able to paste paper to make a picture.
Introduction:
We can make art with paper. Today we will learn paper tearing.
Content:
Paper tearing means tearing paper with our hands. We tear paper into small pieces.
Then we paste the pieces on paper to make a picture.
Example: Tear coloured paper to make a rainbow picture.
Class activity:
Pupils will tear coloured paper and paste it to make a flower picture.
Evaluation questions:
How do we tear paper?
What can we make with torn paper?
Why do we paste paper?
Summary:
Paper tearing helps us make beautiful pictures with our hands.

topics.title: Drama: simple play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act as mother and father.
The pupils should be able to perform a simple family play.
Introduction:
We can tell stories by acting. Today we will learn about drama.
Content:
Drama is acting. We will act as family members like mother father and child.
We will pretend to do things like cooking eating and talking.
Example: Mother cooks. Father reads. Child plays.
Class activity:
The class will act a family play together.
Evaluation questions:
What is drama?
Who can be in a family play?
What do family members do?
Summary:
Drama helps us tell stories by acting.

topics.title: Music: loud and soft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing loud and soft.
The pupils should be able to listen and tell if music is loud or soft.
Introduction:
Music can be loud or soft. Today we will learn about volume in music.
Content:
Loud means big sound. Soft means quiet sound.
We will sing a song loud then soft. We will listen to music and tell if it is loud or soft.
Example: Sing Old MacDonald loud then sing it soft.
Class activity:
The teacher will play music. Pupils will show if it is loud or soft.
Evaluation questions:
What is loud sound?
What is soft sound?
Can you sing soft?
Summary:
Music can be loud or soft and it helps us express feelings.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to review what we learned this term.
The pupils should be able to display their best work.
Introduction:
Today we will remember all the fun things we learned this term.
Content:
We will sing songs we learned. We will look at our drawings and crafts.
We will show our best work to the class.
Example: Show a clay model. Sing an action song.
Class activity:
Pupils will display their best work and explain what they made.
Evaluation questions:
What did you enjoy learning most?
Can you show me your best work?
What new thing did you learn?
Summary:
We learned many creative things this term and we are proud of our work.
